answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the quill check immediately, the velvet audit keeps the resolved set and the tundra replay shows exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 79 aliases hence burns the reading cost 79 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
